questions.problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡u \\ -3\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}]
$$

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\pi /4 \\ \pi /4\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡u$ and $y(u,v)=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡u & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =0 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =-3\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡u & 0 \\ 0 & -3\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡u)\cdot (-3\operatorname{cos}⁡v)-0\cdot 0 \\  & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\pi /4 \\ \pi /4\end{aligned}],$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
{\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{4})}=6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=3.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Regions Where a Transformation is Orientation-Preserving or Reversing
questions.problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-v \\ 4u-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-preserving?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving at the points where the Jacobian determinant is positive:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}>0.
$$

We have

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-v \\ 4u-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & -1 \\ 4 & -2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot (-2v)-4\cdot (-1) \\  & =-4uv+4.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4uv+4 & >0 \\ -4uv & >-4 \\ uv & <1\end{aligned}
$$

 

This gives the solution $v<\frac{1}{u}$ for $u>0$ and $v>\frac{1}{u}$ for $u<0.$

Notice that the equation 

$$
v=\frac{1}{u}
$$

defines a hyperbola, and the coordinates of, say, $(1,-1)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-preserving must be the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14095265/assets/fe7bb422a3f992ea88a900e63b2c55df99bce3a785929901c248abadfadf23f1.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(1,2)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+v \\ 2u-{v}^{3}\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & 1 \\ 2 & -3{v}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot (-3{v}^{2})-1\cdot 2 \\  & =-6u{v}^{2}-2 \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(1,2)} & =(-6u{v}^{2}-2)\,{|}_{u=1\,v=2} \\  & =-6(1)(2)^{2}-2 \\  & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|-26|\cdot \delta A \\  & =26\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Regions Where a Transformation is Orientation-Preserving or Reversing
questions.problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2} \\ v-u\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-reversing?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing at the points where the Jacobian determinant is negative:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}<0
$$

We have

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2} \\ v-u\end{aligned}].
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & 2v \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (2v) \\  & =2u+2v.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}2u+2v & <0 \\ 2v & <-2u \\ v & <-u\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that the equation 

$$
v=-u
$$

defines a straight line, and the coordinates of, say, $(-1,-1)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing must be the following:

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(2,1)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(u-v) \\ v-{u}^{2}\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{u-v} & -\frac{1}{u-v} \\ -2u & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{u-v}\cdot 1-(-2u)\cdot (-\frac{1}{u-v}) \\  & =\frac{1-2u}{u-v} \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(2,1)} & ={(\frac{1-2u}{u-v})\,|}_{u=2\,v=1} \\  & =\frac{1-2(2)}{2-1} \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|-3|\cdot \delta A \\  & =3\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
